issues.legal_issue: An amendment cannot be applied retrospectively to impair vested substantive rights unless that intention is expressed in plain and unmistakable language.
material_facts: The property had been allotted and was subject to proceedings for its division under the applicable rules.
After the relevant rule was deleted by amendment, the property was auctioned and purchased by a third party who deposited the purchase price.
A prior decision held that the amendment could not operate retrospectively in these proceedings, restoring the rule to its original position.
issues.conclusion: The amendment did not apply retrospectively to these proceedings; the auction was quashed and the matter was remitted for partition under the applicable rules.
issues.legal_principle: A statute is not construed retrospectively to take away or impair a vested or substantive right unless that intention is made manifest by plain and unmistakable language. Even where a procedural statute operates retrospectively, it does not affect substantive rights already vested. The Court approved the view in Pt. Dey Ral v. Union of India that the amendment could not retrospectively apply to these proceedings, with the result that Rule 30 was restored for them.

predicates.appeal_from_high_court_judgment: The matter is an appeal from a High Court judgment concerning proceedings to allot or divide property under applicable rules.
predicates.amendment_would_impair_vested_substantiv: Applying an amendment to the proceedings would impair substantive rights that had already vested.
predicates.plain_unmistakable_retroactive_intent: The amendment expresses in plain and unmistakable language an intention to impair those vested substantive rights retrospectively.
predicates.auction_proceedings_are_quashed_and_prop: The auction proceedings are set aside and the property is remitted for partition under the rules applicable to the proceedings.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a High Court judgment concerns an amendment that would impair vested substantive rights and the amendment does not plainly and unmistakably require that result retrospectively, the auction is set aside and the property is remitted for partition under the applicable rules.

issues.legal_issue: An auction purchaser is entitled to repayment with interest when an auction is annulled through no fault of the purchaser.
material_facts: The auction purchaser deposited the purchase price with the authorities.
The auction was annulled because the amendment could not retrospectively govern the property proceedings, and the annulment was through no fault of the purchaser.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser was entitled to a refund of the entire amount deposited with interest at six per cent per annum from the auction date until payment, and the Department was directed to pay it within three months.
issues.legal_principle: In the peculiar circumstances, because the auction had to be annulled through no fault of the purchaser, the Court directed repayment of the deposited purchase price with interest. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this direction.

predicates.auction_annulment_proceeding: The proceeding concerns whether an annulled auction requires repayment to its purchaser.
predicates.purchaser_deposited_purchase_price: The auction purchaser paid the purchase price to the relevant authorities.
predicates.auction_annulled_without_purchaser_fault: The auction was annulled for reasons not attributable to the purchaser.
predicates.purchaser_is_entitled_to_refund_with_int: The purchaser is entitled to repayment of the deposited purchase price together with interest.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns repayment following an annulled auction, the purchaser paid the purchase price, and the annulment was not the purchaser's fault, the purchaser is entitled to repayment with interest.
